name: veterinary_clinic_system_065_deceased_patient_archive
instruction:
A client has just reported that their pet passed away. The patient is not identified by name or id in the call - you must derive it from live data as of the episode date. The deceased patient is the ACTIVE patient with the earliest future scheduled or confirmed appointment (appointment_date >= episode date) among active patients that also have a reserved boarding reservation with check_in >= episode date. If several appointments tie on date, pick the lowest appointment id.

Archive the patient properly and notify the owner:
1. Set the patient's status to 'deceased' and archived='<batch_code>'.
2. Cancel every reserved boarding reservation for that patient with check_in >= episode_date: status='cancelled', cancellation_reason='patient_deceased'.
3. Archive (do not delete) every 'waiting' waitlist entry for that patient: status='archived', archived_by='<batch_code>'.
4. Cancel every future appointment for that patient with status in ('scheduled','confirmed') and appointment_date >= episode_date: status='cancelled'.
5. Push one outbound email to the owner: subject 'Condolences for <patient.name> - <batch_code>', body 'We are sorry to hear that <patient.name> has passed away. We have cancelled future appointments and reservations as of <episode_date>.', channel='email', direction='outbound', logged_by='system', occurred_at the episode timestamp, owner_id and patient_id set.
6. Push one ops_reports row report='deceased_archive', batch_code, patient_id, owner_id, cancelled_reservations, cancelled_appointments, archived_waitlist, archive_note='deceased'.
7. Push one audit_log row: action='PATIENT_DECEASED_ARCHIVED', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='patients', target_id=<patient_id>, details='Batch <batch_code> - archived patient <patient_id>', occurred_at the episode timestamp.

Do not modify completed or past records. Do not change any other patient's data. All mutations must be keyed on the live batch code so a re-run reaches the same end state.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: The target active patient is derived from live data (earliest future scheduled/confirmed appointment among those with a future reserved boarding stay). Patient status becomes 'deceased' with archived=batch. Future reserved boarding stays for that patient become 'cancelled' with cancellation_reason='patient_deceased'. Future scheduled/confirmed appointments become 'cancelled'. Waiting waitlist entries for that patient become 'archived' with archived_by=batch. Exactly one condolence communication is pushed. Exactly one ops_reports row and one audit_log row are created for the batch. All other rows across the seven collections are unchanged (or, for ops_reports/audit_log/communications, only the expected new rows).

checks.expect: Target patient derived from live data; all cancellations and archive tags match; communications/ops_reports/audit_log counts and content verified.
Target selection and cancellation counts are computed independently via Python filter and SQL and must agree.

hazards: Patient 17 (Rocket, owner 13) was the v1 target but is now active with no future scheduled/confirmed appointments or reserved boarding stays in the v2 seed; a hardcoded id 17 archives the wrong patient and fails (patient id 17, status 'active', weight 6, location 1).

The actual target is episode-date dependent: at 2026-09-27/28 the target is patient 1 (Biscuit, owner 1, appointment 227 on 2026-09-28, boarding reservation 83 check_in 2026-11-02); at 2026-09-29 the target is patient 200 (Bailey, owner 211, appointment 66 on 2026-09-29, reservation 20 check_in 2026-10-27); at 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-03 the target is patient 204 (Millie, owner 36, appointment 418 on 2026-10-03, reservation 81 check_in 2026-10-31). A hardcoded id fails on other episode dates.

There are 7 reserved boarding reservations with check_in before the episode date (ids 6, 7, 8, 17, 65, 85, 98, all with check_in on 2026-09-24 or earlier). A cancellation that does not require check_in >= episode_date will over-cancel and fail.

Appointments include past/completed/checked_in/no_show statuses (176 completed, 66 no_show, 10 checked_in in the seed). Cancelling all appointments for the target regardless of status or date alters history and fails.
The waitlist has 6 rows for patients 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, and 23. Only the target patient's waiting rows may be archived; deleting all waiting rows or deleting other patients' rows fails.
The target selection rule requires BOTH a future scheduled/confirmed appointment and a future reserved boarding stay. A patient with only one or the other must not be selected.
